description: We are a team of passionate innovators exploring the power of AI, satellite technology, and geospatial intelligence to understand Earth's changing surface. We aim to turn real-world satellite data into meaningful insights through innovative technology and collaboration.
summary: What can satellites reveal about a changing lagoon—and where does the evidence stop? CHRONO EARTH turns real Earth observations into a time journey through Chilika Lagoon, Odisha. Its Time Stone opens REWIND, where visitors explore 25 Sentinel-1 radar and 25 Landsat optical observations from 2015–2026; WITNESS, which presents a real NISAR radar pass from November 6, 2026; and EXPLORE, which compares actual dry-season and monsoon-season observations. Radar and optical measurements remain distinct, and candidate water indicators are clearly labeled as unvalidated. Because the historical record is sparse and lacks independent, date-matched ground truth, CHRONO EARTH does not claim to forecast future conditions. Instead, it makes satellite evidence easier to explore and helps researchers, educators, and wetland managers ask better questions about seasonal change.
details:
CHRONO EARTH turns satellite observations of Chilika Lagoon into an interactive journey through time. The Time Stone opens three experiences: REWIND compares 25 Sentinel-1 radar and 25 Landsat optical observations from 2015–2026; WITNESS presents a real NISAR L-band observation from November 6, 2026; and EXPLORE compares actual dry-season and monsoon-season observations as historical what-if scenarios.

The project displays radar backscatter and Landsat NDVI, NDWI, and MNDWI as distinct measurements. It makes coverage, data quality, and uncertainty visible: candidate water indicators are unvalidated, NDVI is not a vegetation classification, and sparse observations without independent ground truth are not enough to forecast future conditions. The app does not claim measured community impacts.

Our creative approach uses the Time Stone to make a complex satellite archive easier to explore. We built the frontend with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, and the analysis pipeline with Python and geospatial libraries including Rasterio, Shapely, NumPy, and SciPy. We considered seasonal gaps, cloud and quality masks, spatial coverage, differences between radar and optical sensors, and the limits of validation. CHRONO EARTH is designed as a clear starting point for researchers, educators, and wetland managers to ask better questions about seasonal change.
